## Highlights since 0.15.4

- **Every Overleaf project you can open.** The import list shows all your Overleaf projects in Overleaf's own order with each owner, plus invitations you have not accepted yet, with Open invitation. You can also paste an Overleaf project or share link to open it, and you are told clearly when it needs joining, an accepted invitation or access.
- **The AI assistant says what went wrong.** When Claude Code cannot start, the card says why and what to do, such as updating a Claude Code older than 2.0.63 or signing in. A model your account cannot use is greyed out with the reason, and the composer switches to the default model with a notice. An Anthropic 403 refusal gets its own message, and warnings show next to the composer.

## Notable fixes

- The Overleaf sign-in window has a Back to Overleaf sign-in button on Google, ORCID, IEEE and SSO pages.
- Check references proposes references and field names in English in any interface language, no longer sticks the tag to the next word, no longer proposes braces around a whole title, and no longer names an undated paper NIPS. A note says that closing the window does not stop the check.
- Annotation pins on the PDF match the size of the source gutter's pins and scale with the zoom.
- The editor runs on Tiptap 3.33.0, and presentations on the latest Open Slide.
- Developer builds give the performance lab its own test keychain.
